testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

survived.claim: costGuardFault's new shape check for `tripped` entries only checks for a string `cell`. Before the PR, the same input returned a fault string. Now an entry whose `on` is a number makes costGuardFault and readCostGuard throw TypeError. An `on` that is a string or names an unknown reason passes as a valid guard, though the router's parseGuard refuses that same file.
survived.evidence: In the copy: costGuardFault on {verdict:'tripped',…,tripped:[{cell:'task-high',on:5}]} printed `THREW number 5 is not iterable`. readCostGuard('badguard.json') on that file printed `THREW TypeError number 5 is not iterable`. probe1.mjs: [{cell:'task-high',on:'usd'}] gives tick `null` but router `{ok:false, why:'`tripped` names task-high on "usd", which is not a list of floor, usd, minutes'}`; on:['bogus'] gives the same split. routerRows on the on:'usd' guard printed `cost guard: task-high (u, s, d) $2.00 vs $1.00 …`. readCostGuard is called with no try at fleet-tick.mjs:2450 (tick main) and at board-gather.mjs:834, whose comment says `none of them throws`. The grep for tripFault in fleet-tick.mjs finds only the import at line 1762: it is imported and never called.
survived.suggested_fix: In costGuardFault, validate entries with the imported tripFault, e.g. `const fault = Array.isArray(guard.tripped) ? guard.tripped.map(tripFault).find((w) => w !== null) : "`tripped` is not a list"; if (fault) return fault;`, before any tripEntry call. The tick then refuses exactly what the router refuses.

votes.reason: Ran costGuardFault imported straight from the snapshot's plugin/scripts/fleet-tick.mjs (read-only import, probe in scratch). With a tripped entry {cell:'task-high',on:5} it THREW 'number 5 is not iterable'. With on:'usd' and on:['bogus'] it returned null, i.e. accepted as a valid guard. The shape check at line 573 only tests a string `cell`. trip-reasons.mjs tripFault, which would reject these, is imported at line 1762 but not used in costGuardFault, and the router's check is the one that refuses them. Not run: readCostGuard's callers, the pre-PR behaviour, and the test suite; the throw follows from costGuardFault, which readCostGuard calls without a try. No mutant was applied, so no red/baseline line. survived.claim: definedCells() swallows every readdirSync failure into an empty Set, so an unlistable agents directory makes every Cell look undefined and phase 0 blames the user's valid saved/--baseline-cell value as 'not a Cell with an implementer definition' instead of reporting the unreadable directory.
survived.evidence: Probe in copy: definedCells('/nonexistent/agents').size -> 0; readSavedBaseline(dirWith{"cell":"slow-low"}, thatSet) -> {state:'invalid', why:'.../baseline-cell.json names "slow-low", which is not a Cell with an implementer definition'}; resolveBaselineCell({arg:'slow-low', saved, defined}) -> cell 'slow-high', notices: '--baseline-cell "slow-low" is not a Cell with an implementer definition: ignored, and not saved' plus 'the saved Baseline Cell is invalid (...)'. With the real defined set the same file reads {state:'ok', cell:'slow-low'}. The fault is mislabelled, the valid value is dropped, and no stderr says the agents dir could not be read.
survived.suggested_fix: Let definedCells throw on non-ENOENT errors, or return {set, why} and have readSavedBaseline/resolveBaselineCell/phase0 say 'cannot list <agents dir>: <code>' rather than blaming the value.

votes.reason: Confirmed by reading the snapshot source only. Its doc comment says 'empty when the directory cannot be listed'. readSavedBaseline (line 54) then reports a saved valid cell as 'not a Cell with an implementer definition' when that set is empty. phase0.mjs:755 calls definedCells() with the default shipped agents directory and no error reporting. The behaviour is as claimed, but the trigger is a broken install (missing shipped agents dir), so the practical impact is small. refuted.claim: baselineOf (used by baselineIn for pr-cost --guard, metrics-refresh, cell-readout, board-gather and ticket-router's receipt path) silently changes the Baseline Cell when the receipt is unreadable/corrupt, records an invalid string, or the saved file is invalid, with no notice or stderr, so the persisted cost guard is computed and written under a different baseline than the run's.
refuted.evidence: Probe baselineIn(dir): receipt {baselineCell:'bogus'} + saved slow-low -> {cell:'slow-low', source:'the saved value'}; receipt '{corrupt' + saved slow-low -> same; both corrupt -> {cell:'slow-high', source:'the default'}. End to end with a gh stub: fleet dir with phase0.json='{corrupt' and baseline-cell.json={"cell":"smol-low"}, `pr-cost.mjs --guard --out <fleet>/cost-guard.json` wrote baseline.cell 'smol-low' with empty stderr; then baseline-cell.json='{corrupt' -> guard written with baseline.cell 'slow-high', empty stderr. readSavedBaseline's `why` and readReceipt's `why` are discarded on these paths. A resumed phase 0 exits 3 on the same bogus receipt value, so the readers are inconsistent with the writer.
refuted.suggested_fix: Have baselineOf return its reasons (receipt/saved `why`) and have the CLI callers (pr-cost, metrics-refresh, ticket-router, cell-readout) write them to stderr, or refuse when the receipt exists but is unreadable or records a non-Cell, as phase0 does.

votes.reason: I read the code and did not run it, so there is no run evidence line. baselineOf (phase0-receipt.mjs:177-185) falls through to the saved value, then to DEFAULT_BASELINE_CELL, when the receipt is unreadable or records a non-CELL string. It does the same when the saved file is invalid. readReceipt's and readSavedBaseline's `why` are never used on those paths. Every caller I found in plugin/scripts uses only `.cell` and drops `.source`: board-gather:1342, cell-readout:185, metrics-refresh:425, pr-cost:510, and ticket-router:1251 (via baselineCellFromReceipt). Only phase0.mjs:946 prints the source, and that is the writer. So the silent fallback is as the claim describes. The doc comment says the fallthrough is deliberate ("Never throws, and never refuses"), which weakens it as a defect. The silence itself is not documented. I did not reproduce the end-to-end pr-cost --guard run. CWD-AUDIT: not run (the `pwd` and shell commands errored in this environment, so the working directory was never recorded).

The behavior is real but deliberate and documented, not a silent-failure bug. The baselineOf docstring (phase0-receipt.mjs:170-176) says the chain is receipt, then saved value, then default, and that it 'Never throws, and never refuses: a reader that cannot be told the Cell runs the default'. baselineOf also returns a `source` field ('the saved value', 'the default') so the fallback is labelled. The evidence shows the fallback chain working as written, which is weaker than the claim of a defect.
